It's officially election day.

History says stocks are heading higher.

In fact, the S&P 500 has closed GREEN in the year following every US Midterm election since 1980.

As we noted in our analysis yesterday, we believe recent weakness in markets is largely a function of the uncertainty around Midterm elections.

However, when this uncertainty dissipates, markets react positively.

Since 1980, the S&P 500 has averaged a +14% gain in the 12 months following US Midterm elections.

Furthermore, even after divided-government outcomes, the index has averaged a +15% one-year gain, compared to +12% under single-party control.

Of course, the near-term picture will come with volatility and change.

But, if history is any guide, it's a great time to be bullish.

Turn on our post notifications at @KobeissiLetter for real-time analysis as this develops.

AI infrastructure spending is driving a sharp increase in US bank lending:

Commercial and Industrial (C&I) loans at large US banks surged +11.4% YoY in October, to $1.6 trillion, the most since June 2020.

This also marked their largest YoY growth since February 2023.

In Q3, C&I loans at the 25 largest US banks grew almost +10.0% YoY, the strongest growth in 10 years excluding pandemic-related swings.

This represents a sharp reversal from an -8.0% YoY contraction in Q4 2025.

The surge has been driven by rising borrowing demand from Big Tech companies and data-center developers to fund AI infrastructure projects.

At the same time, regional lenders are providing credit to construction companies and other businesses benefiting from the investment boom.

The data-center buildout is increasingly being funded by debt.

BREAKING: Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, Microsoft, $MSFT, Amazon, $AMZN, and Oracle, $ORCL, have now disclosed a record $3.3 trillion in future spending commitments.

These are off-balance-sheet commitments covering data-center spending, future equipment purchases, leases, and other obligations.

$GOOGL accounts for the largest amount at $1.06 trillion, with its disclosed commitments surging nearly +700% over the last year.

$META follows at $866 billion, with nearly half tied to data-center leases that have not yet commenced and payment periods extending up to 30 years.

Meanwhile, Microsoft, $MSFT, has $593 billion in commitments, followed by Amazon, $AMZN, at $453 billion, and Oracle, $ORCL, at $322 billion.

The AI infrastructure buildout is creating an unprecedented pipeline of future financial obligations.

What's happening now in the stock market is more than just a "correction in tech stocks."

Sure, AI CapEx concerns are legitimate and investors will always care about profitability.

But, there's more beneath the surface here.

The reality is that the market is pricing-in a major shift in the political landscape of the US.

Over the last 12 months, market expectations for a Democrat "sweep" of the US Midterm elections have tripled.

Over the last 45 days alone, these expectations are up +30 percentage points.

As it stands, markets themselves now see a near-80% chance of a Democrat "sweep" of the US Midterm elections.

President Trump has already vowed to become "Mr. Veto" if this in fact does happen.

This is post is not political, it's objective. A change in the political landscape always comes with uncertainty; markets hate uncertainty. 

Objectively, the market is in the process of pricing-in two years of political gridlock.

Could this change? Of course. But markets price-in the most probable outcome, and the odds now overwhelmingly favor the aforementioned scenario.

Tomorrow sets the stage for the next two years.

Markets are heading into their strongest seasonal period of the year:

Since 1980, the S&P 500 has rallied +2.1% on average in November, making it the strongest month of the year.

Over this period, positive returns occurred 74% of the time, the best hit rate of any month.

Furthermore, the S&P 500 has gained +1.6% on average in November since 1964, with positive returns occurring 69% of the time.

The highest November return during this period was +10.8%, recorded in 2020.

During midterm years, November has averaged +2.7% since 1950, with a 78.9% win rate.

History points to a strong month ahead.
